persons.name: Leslie
persons.harm: Over about four months in 2010 her boyfriend love-bombed, isolated, monitored, lied to and financially leaned on her, gaslighting her about his protective-order history and about injuries to her adopted son; on 12-13 June 2010, while she worked a night shift, he fatally beat her three-year-old son Jace.
persons.perpetrator_role: her live-in boyfriend (met through online dating)

quotes.quote: If I ever confronted him about anything throughout our relationship, by the end of the conversation, I would feel guilty about ever even doubting him. Gaslighting at its finest.
I never thought he would hurt me or Jace, but I was afraid he would threaten to kill himself and he would never leave me alone.

contacts.institution: Tulsa Police Department (patrol officers, then child crisis unit detective)
contacts.when: morning of 13 June 2010, at the hospital
contacts.what_institution_did: Patrol officers and the lead detective interviewed her at the hospital; the detective judged she was not involved and focused the investigation on the boyfriend.
contacts.quote: when I met Leslie, my gut was like, okay, I really don't think she's involved. It seems like she really was taking steps to try to figure out and get to the bottom of these injuries, but somehow he kind of fell through the cracks, honestly.
contacts.what_happened_next: Investigation proceeded against the boyfriend; Leslie says the detective was 'the only one who finally helped me accept that [perpetrator] did this'.
contacts.notes: Leslie: 'She did her job well and treated everyone with respect.' (s17-e3 @ 31:54)

contacts.institution: Department of Human Services, Child Protective Services (protective custody placed by the detective)
contacts.what_institution_did: Jace was placed in protective custody and Leslie was barred from the hospital while her son lay dying, because she was one of only two caregivers in the injury window.
contacts.quote: They wouldn't allow Leslie to be at the hospital. The Department of Human Services, Child Protective Services was involved, so they wouldn't allow her to be at the hospital.
contacts.what_happened_next: She had to go before a judge two days later to be allowed back.
contacts.notes: Detective: 'So I had to place Jason protective custody. So I basically had to kick Leslie out of the hospital and make her leave' (s17-e3 @ 24:46). The detective presents it as procedure; the quote shows exclusion of the mother, not an explicit accusation. Lauren: 'they have to question her. Did you know about this? Really making her feel like a crappy parent?' (s17-e3 @ 15:29). Could also be read as acted_partly/protective procedure.

contacts.what_was_asked: To be allowed to be with her son at the hospital
contacts.what_institution_did: The judge allowed her back at the hospital.
contacts.quote: She had to go before a judge two days later and the judge then allowed her to be at the hospital.
contacts.what_happened_next: She was present when life support was withdrawn; Jace died 16 June 2010.

contacts.what_institution_did: The DA's office issued an arrest warrant for first-degree murder on the detective's application.
contacts.quote: Short time after that, I typed up an arrest warrant. I presented it to the District Attorney's Office and they issued a warrant for his arrest for first degree murder.
contacts.what_happened_next: Boyfriend arrested 23 June 2010.

contacts.institution: fugitive warrant squad / Payne County deputies
contacts.what_institution_did: Deputies arrested him near Stillwater and he was returned to Tulsa and jailed.
contacts.quote: And once the warrant was issued, I had our fugitive warrant squad contact. I believe it was Payne County. And they actually went and arrested him on June 23.
contacts.what_happened_next: He stayed in jail until trial, but kept contacting Leslie through his sister ('He was still trying to manipulate me through her.' s17-e3 @ 42:14).
contacts.notes: News clip read on air confirms the arrest (s17-e3 @ 41:12).

contacts.institution: Tulsa County District Attorney's Office (trial prosecutors)
contacts.what_institution_did: In closing, the prosecutor openly blamed Leslie's judgment (while arguing that did not lessen his guilt).
contacts.quote: Probably the biggest what if in this case is Leslie. How could somebody so smart be so dumb? You know, when you're single parent, you're not just responsible for yourself, you're responsible for that little life.
contacts.what_happened_next: Leslie: 'That was very hard to hear, but it was also true.' Conviction followed.
contacts.notes: Read on air by Leslie from the trial transcript. The prosecutors were otherwise described as supportive ('She never came at us with accusations', s17-e4 @ 5:14); earlier the DA once seemed to question her motive for printing texts (s17-e4 @ 4:11). Main prosecutorial response was believed_and_acted; this contact records the blame.

contacts.what_institution_did: The jury found him guilty of first-degree child abuse murder and fixed punishment at life and a $10,000 fine.
contacts.quote: We the jury, and paneled and sworn in the above titled cause, do upon our oaths, find as follows. The defendant is guilty and fixed punishment at life and a fine of $10,000.
contacts.what_happened_next: Sentenced in April 2012 to life with the possibility of parole; Leslie read her victim impact statement.

contacts.institution: Tulsa County District Court (sentencing) and appellate courts
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge imposed life with the possibility of parole (minimum 38 years before parole consideration); appeals and post-conviction requests were denied.
contacts.quote: He tried that at least three times, which was denied by the judge. He tried two appeals, which were denied, and he has no other options. This is his life now.
contacts.what_happened_next: He remains in prison.

persons.outcome_quote: but I take solace and knowing you will never have the opportunity to hurt another child. Never be able to manipulate and control another woman and I don't ever want to speak your name again.
persons.decisive_work_quote: he was the only one with Jay's from about 7 p.m. that the night on the 12th until 130 in the morning on the 13th when 911 was called by his own statements. Nobody else was there.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: same day: police investigation began the morning Jace was admitted (13 June 2010); arrest 10 days later
persons.notes: Her coercive-control harm never reached an institution before the murder; the institutions engaged only after Jace was fatally injured. Arrest and life sentence ended his access to her, but the harm she sought protection from (her son's safety) was not prevented, he kept manipulating her via his sister while jailed, and his family accused her online and as late as the podcast (s17-ep6-healer @ 37:14). Outcome partly_protected rather than protected for that reason; a coder could argue protected (conviction delivered) or not_protected (relationship harm ended because of the murder, not an institution). harmed_by_institution_ever=true rests on the DHS hospital exclusion and the prosecutor's closing blame; both are arguable. Leslie's counselor and the police told the family it was not her fault (s17-e3 @ 45:17). Leslie asked the DA about suing the ER doctor; DA said she did not think he would be found liable (s17-e4 @ 44:29).

persons.name: Jace
persons.harm: Three-year-old adopted son of Leslie; over roughly two months in spring 2010 he showed repeated unexplained injuries (bilateral ear bruising, wrist marks, a head bump) while in the boyfriend's care and said the boyfriend hurt/shook him; on 12-13 June 2010 the boyfriend inflicted fatal blunt force head trauma and he died 16 June 2010.

quotes.quote: And so I even called my other friends who were also social workers. Like, what do I need to do? And they were like, well, I guess if the doctor says it's nothing to worry about, I wouldn't worry about it.
I couldn't even entertain that thought.

But when you're talking about your own family, it makes it a little bit more difficult. And then you narrow it down, and you've been a part of the system. And you know exactly what you're going to be asked. It makes it even more difficult.

contacts.institution: emergency room at the hospital where Leslie worked (ER physician)
contacts.when: spring 2010 (about April-May), after 10 pm, the night ear bruising appeared
contacts.what_was_asked: Assessment of bilateral bruising inside both ears (possible skull fracture)
contacts.what_institution_did: Did a limited neuro exam, asked who had watched Jace, offered an optional CT, and sent him home; he charted that it looked like Jace had been slapped on both sides of the head but made no child-abuse report.
contacts.quote: Later, I would find out he documented in his notes in the official legal chart that it appeared to be child abuse, like someone slapped Jace on both sides of his head. but there was no social worker on site during the night, so he would let the pediatrician follow up.
contacts.what_happened_next: Jace went home with Leslie and the boyfriend; pediatrician follow-up next day.
contacts.notes: Leslie later reads the chart note on air (s17-e4 @ 44:29): 'it would appear like the patient was slapped simultaneously on bilateral sides of the head'. Detective: those doctors 'regret decisions that they made sending Jason. back home. They testified to that.' (s17-ep6 @ 7:13).

contacts.what_was_asked: Explanation of the ear bruising (Stacey had urged that abuse was the only explanation)
contacts.what_institution_did: Tested for a bleeding disorder (ruled out) and said to watch it; did not raise abuse or report.
contacts.quote: I made my sister take him to the doctor. I'm like, Leslie, this is the only explanation that anyone can find. But the pediatricians said they weren't worried about it.
contacts.what_happened_next: No report; Jace stayed in the home.
contacts.notes: Leslie: 'The only reasonable explanation they could come up with was some kind of bleeding disorder. We did testing for that, it was ruled out. We would just have to watch it.' (s17-e2 @ 38:00-39:04). Testing could support acted_partly. Detective: 'They took him to the doctor, and they pretty much got dismissed.' (s17-e3 @ 27:50). The boyfriend was present at this visit.

contacts.what_was_asked: Leslie raised the ear bruising at an unrelated follow-up
contacts.what_institution_did: Suggested he was sleeping on his ears wrong; no abuse concern raised.
contacts.quote: I brought up the bruising, thinking he might have some insight. Stop, maybe he was sleeping on his ears wrong. No one brought up child abuse.
contacts.what_happened_next: No action; further injuries followed (wrist marks; '[perpetrator] shaped me').
contacts.notes: Benign explanation could also be read as disbelieved.

contacts.institution: St. Francis Hospital (ER, neurosurgery, child abuse team)
contacts.what_was_asked: Emergency care (boyfriend called 911 claiming a fall from bed)
contacts.what_institution_did: Doctors treated the brain injury, recognised abuse and law enforcement was called.
contacts.quote: As soon as Jace shows up at the hospital with his massive brain injury and covered in bruises, of course, law enforcement is called.
contacts.what_happened_next: Police and DHS involved; Jace declared brain dead; organs donated; died 16 June 2010.
contacts.notes: Tulsa Fire Department first responder noticed 'something wasn't right' (s17-e4 @ 23:41).

contacts.institution: Tulsa Police Department (patrol, child crisis unit)
contacts.what_institution_did: Officers interviewed family; Stacey told them of his history with the other child; detectives investigated, photographed injuries and home.
contacts.quote: They say, yeah, we were kind of wondering about that, and we'll have the detectives talk to you as soon as they get here. Then a couple of detectives come, and they talk to me first, and I tell them the situation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Investigation focused on the boyfriend; he left the hospital and took the TV.

contacts.quote: So I had to place Jason protective custody.
contacts.what_happened_next: He died three days later.

contacts.what_happened_next: Jailed until trial.

contacts.what_institution_did: Guilty of child abuse murder in the first degree; life and $10,000 fine.
contacts.quote: We the jury, and paneled and sworn in the above titled cause, do upon our oaths, find as follows. The defendant is guilty and fixed punishment at life and a fine of $10,000.
contacts.what_happened_next: Sentenced April 2012.

contacts.what_institution_did: Life with possibility of parole; two appeals and other post-conviction attempts denied.

contacts.what_happened_next: Appeals denied (s17-ep6 @ 39:17).

persons.outcome_quote: And I'm not that I'm blaming them, but I feel like the people that were speaking the loudest for him weren't really being heard at that time with their concerns and I really believe something could have maybe changed the outcome of this case if somebody would have just listened to them, he ended up getting murdered before anybody really listened.
persons.notes: Died of the harm; conviction recorded as contacts but is not protection. Three medical contacts (ER, pediatrician, ENT) before death; none reported to child protection. The detective and the prosecutor's closing both say a referral might have saved him (s17-e3 @ 27:50; s17-e5 @ 20:22). Exact dates of the ER/pediatrician visits not given; ER visit followed a ride-on-car 'accident' and Leslie had already booked a pediatrician appointment. Stacey suggests the pediatrician was seen about the ears; Leslie's and Stacey's accounts appear to describe the same pediatrician visit. Stacey never called DHS ('I wish I had called DHS', s17-e4 @ 47:36). harmed_by_institution_ever kept false: the doctors' failures are coded did_nothing/disbelieved, not active endangerment, though the ER physician sending him home after charting suspected abuse could be argued as endangerment.

persons.name: Jace (birth mother)
persons.harm: Born at 25 weeks to a mother with a drug-use problem who had lost custody of six earlier children; the show presents his prematurity and early condition as linked to her drug use.

contacts.what_institution_did: Placed him in protective custody; he was later fostered and adopted by Leslie (finalised 20 March 2009).

persons.harm: As a high-school senior she was drawn into a charismatic house church run by a classmate's family that became a controlling cult; she cut off her family for about a year, gave the group money, and was later shunned by it.

quotes.quote: As far as things like mind control and cults and things like that, I was in it. And if they would have said, God wants you to jump off a bridge and kill yourself, I would have said, okay, I have no doubt in my mind that I would have done it.

coder_notes: Season 17 (Something Was Wrong): Leslie, her adopted son Jace (murdered June 2010 by Leslie's boyfriend), and her sister Stacey; plus the boyfriend's earlier victims (Samantha and her infant daughter, Samantha's sister, a 2010 ex and her friend). The final chunk ends with a generic 'Data Points: Child Abuse' episode with statistics only and no person stories. I read unassigned/INDEX.txt; no listed episode appeared to continue or discuss the S17 story (all are generic data-point or unrelated episodes), so I opened none. The perpetrator's name is replaced with [perpetrator] in quotes. Main judgment calls: Leslie's outcome (partly_protected) and harmed_by_institution_ever (DHS hospital exclusion; prosecutor's closing blame); whether Jace (birth mother) and the thin protective-order records (P09-P11) should be persons or others_mentioned; Stacey's three records split by perpetrator. Leslie's adolescent anorexia and Leslie being left behind when Stacey joined the cult are not coded because they have no perpetrator. Reading was interrupted twice by usage limits and resumed from the notes file; every file was read to its last line.
